claims.text: The initial HfNbTiVAl10 material has a hierarchical heterostructure.
A hybrid machine-learning and DFT approach can accurately predict Young's modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A hybrid machine-learning and DFT approach can accurately predict yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A hybrid machine-learning and DFT approach can accurately predict toughness under fracture testing for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The hybrid approach will reduce computational demands relative to the listed prior methods.
The hybrid approach will increase prediction efficiency relative to the listed prior methods.
Use of a high-performance computing cluster is a condition for the proposed approach.
The proposed approach requires a dataset of at least 1000 calculated structures and associated properties.
Chemical fluctuations and short-range order are the structural mediators relevant to the predicted mechanical properties.
Machine-learning models trained on DFT-calculated properties can capture relationships between chemical fluctuations, short-range order, and mechanical properties.
Failure to validate and test the machine-learning models carefully may make the approach unreliable.
Insufficient computational resources may make the approach unreliable.
Rigorous validation and testing protocols may reduce uncertainty in the predicted mechanical properties.
The proposed benchmark will prospectively and blindly compare predictions with experimental Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
